title: Noetherian relation schemes of affine etale atlases
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Locally Noetherian means that every etale scheme chart is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; Noetherian means locally Noetherian, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, with quasi-separated meaning that the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Assume $X$ is Noetherian and let $p:U\to X$ be a representable surjective etale map with $U$ affine. Here affine means a spectrum of a commutative ring. Put $R=U\times_XU$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $s,t:R\to U$ and the usual identity, inverse and composition maps. Then these maps form a groupoid scheme [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]; $U$ and $R$ are Noetherian schemes, and $s,t$ are etale, flat, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Etale is [def-weil-etale-morphism], flat is [def-weil-flat-morphism], quasi-compact means quasi-compact inverse images of affine opens, and quasi-separated means a quasi-compact diagonal. No separatedness of $X$ over $S$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03EA (definition-noetherian), Tag 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover); properties of the chosen presentation in the proof of spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 07UV (lemma-directed-colimit-coherent); spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0467 (lemma-etale-flat).

proof.text: By representability of $p$, its pullback along $U\to X$ is a scheme $R$, and both projections $s,t:R\to U$ are etale scheme morphisms: each is a scheme test of $p$ (the two are exchanged by the swap $(a,b)\mapsto(b,a)$). In particular they are flat by the definition of etale. As $U\to X$ is an etale scheme chart, $U$ is locally Noetherian by the hypothesis on $X$. The chartwise etale permanence lemma identifies representable etale maps with chartwise etale maps when the source is a scheme, makes base changes of chartwise etale maps chartwise etale, and makes their composites chartwise etale. Hence $p$ is chartwise etale, its base change $s:R=U\times_XU\to U$ along $p$ is chartwise etale, and so $p\circ s:R\to X$ is chartwise etale; its source is a scheme, so it is representable etale. Consequently $R$ is also an etale scheme chart of $X$ and is locally Noetherian. Neither this argument nor the definition of a chart requires the chart to be surjective.

source.place: Tags 03FR (definition-etale), 03FT (lemma-composition-etale); locally Noetherian is an etale-local scheme property, section-types-properties; spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 07UV (lemma-directed-colimit-coherent), chosen presentation.

proof.text: Choose the convention $t(a,b)=a$, $s(a,b)=b$ on $R(T)=\{(a,b)\in U(T)^2:p(a)=p(b)\}$. Define $e(a)=(a,a)$, $i(a,b)=(b,a)$ and $c((a,b),(b,d))=(a,d)$. The fibre-product universal property gives these scheme morphisms: for composition the first and last components have the same image in $X$, since their images both equal that of the middle component. Source and target of a composite are its last and first components. Identities and inverse identities reduce respectively to deleting a repeated component and to $(a,a)$ or $(b,b)$. Both parenthesizations of a composable triple give the pair of its first and last components, proving associativity. These operations commute with precomposition on $T$; hence they give all the groupoid laws in the cited definition.

source.place: Tag 0231 (definition-groupoid), groupoid axioms preceding the definition; Tag 0233 (lemma-equivalence-groupoid), with the elementary verification written here.

proof.text: For a scheme $T$ the point space $|h_T|$ of [def-a1-space-point-topology] is $|T|$ with its Zariski topology: a point $x$ gives the class of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to T$, every field-valued point of $T$ is equivalent to exactly one of these (its image point), the identity of $T$ is one of the test maps, so open sets of $|h_T|$ are Zariski open, and conversely every representable etale $h_{T'}\to h_T$ is a scheme morphism $T'\to T$, hence continuous. Thus quasi-compactness of $T$ as a scheme and as an algebraic space agree. The affine-scheme lemma makes $U$ quasi-compact; it is also quasi-separated as an algebraic space, since for affine schemes $T,T'$ mapping to the affine scheme $U$ the product $T\times_UT'$ is affine by the affine fibre-product lemma, hence quasi-compact. The hypothesis that $X$ is Noetherian makes $X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated (the diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, which is the quasi-separatedness used by the two qcqs lemmas). Apply the qcqs fibre-product lemma with $A=B=U$, $C=X$ and both structure maps equal to $p$. It gives that $R=U\times_XU$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated as an algebraic space, in particular a quasi-compact scheme. Combining quasi-compactness of $U$ and $R$ with their local Noetherianity proved in step 1 shows that both are Noetherian schemes (for schemes this means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact). The fibre-product lemma explicitly imposes no compactness or separation hypothesis on the ambient scheme $S$.

source.place: Tag 073B (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence), clause (3); spaces-properties.tex Tag 03EA (definition-noetherian) and following paragraph.

proof.text: Apply qcqs permanence separately to $s:R\to U$ and $t:R\to U$, viewed as morphisms of algebraic spaces: the source $R$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by step 3, and the target $U$ is quasi-separated by the same step. Each projection is therefore quasi-compact and quasi-separated in the sense of that lemma. These give the scheme meanings in the item: for an affine open $V\subseteq U$, the base change $V\times_UR$ is the open subscheme $s^{-1}(V)$, whose point space is quasi-compact, so $s^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact by the identification of step 3; likewise the relative diagonal $R\to R\times_UR$ (a scheme fibre product, as $R\to U$ is a scheme map) has quasi-compact base change along every affine open of $R\times_UR$, i.e. it is a quasi-compact morphism of schemes. Together with the etale and flat conclusions of step 1 and the groupoid structure of step 2, this proves every assertion.

lean.statement: theorem noetherian_affine_atlas_relation {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hln : ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, IsLocallyNoetherian (X.etaleForget.obj T)) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : ∀ (V W : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsAffine V.left → IsAffine W.left → CompactSpace (Point (Limits.pullback a b))) (U : Over S) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (hp : IsEtale p) (hsurj : IsSurjective p) (haff : IsAffine U.left) : IsNoetherian U.left ∧ ∃ (R : Over S) (t s : R ⟶ U), IsPullback (yoneda.map t) (yoneda.map s) p p ∧ IsNoetherian R.left ∧ Etale s.left ∧ Etale t.left ∧ Flat s.left ∧ Flat t.left ∧ QuasiCompact s.left ∧ QuasiCompact t.left ∧ QuasiSeparated s.left ∧ QuasiSeparated t.left ∧ ∃ (e : U.left ⟶ R.left) (i : R.left ⟶ R.left) (c : Limits.pullback s.left t.left ⟶ R.left), Scheme.IsGroupoid s.left t.left e i c
